newsitem.title: USA: SEC denies Stratton bid for stay of NASD expulsion.
newsitem.headline: SEC denies Stratton bid for stay of NASD expulsion.

text.p: The Securities and Exchange Commission said Monday it had denied a request by Stratton Oakmont Inc for a stay of a National Association of Securities Dealers order expelling the firm from the securities industry.
The SEC also denied a separate bid for a stay requested by Daniel Porush, president of the brokerage, who was censured and barred from the securities industry by the NASD.
The NASD's regulatory arm issued the sanctions December 5. They stemmed from charges of excessive and fraudulent markups and failure to supervise in connection with a 1993 initial public offering.
The NASD unit also took into account a string of disciplinary actions it and other regulators have taken against the New York-based brokerage in imposing the sanctions.

In issuing its action, the SEC said the expulsion shall not be effective for five business days from December 6, the date of its order, so that Stratton may carry out liquidating transactions for its customers.
In its order, the SEC said:

"Under the circumstances, any harm that Applicants may incur from the denial of their stay requests is outweighed by the danger to the investing public if the effect of the bar and the expulsion is delayed. We therefore determine that it is in the public interest to deny the request for stays."
As part of its sanctions, the NASD censured and fined the firm $500,000 and ordered it to make restitution of $416,529 to customers.
In addition to being barred form the securities industry, Porush was also censured and fined $250,000.
